names.note: Name page of days.pravoslavie.ru for this memory is «Святитель Досифей (Васич), митрополит Загребский, исповедник»: «Святитель», «митрополит», the see and «исповедник» are rank words and are stripped, the surname kept. The form is stored in the RUSSIAN spelling the calendar prints, «Васич», and not in a Serbian one, which this reader has not seen. The day line itself gives only «Досифея , митр. Загребского, исп». `fk.mjs` on the stored string returns NONE.

death.note: The day line closes «(1945)», which is the whole of what the source gives; no year of birth anywhere.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 31 декабря ст. ст. — «Свт. Досифея , митр. Загребского, исп (1945).»

attestations.note: The day’s fifth entry, and THE LINE AND THE NAME PAGE ARE ALL THERE IS: no life page stands behind it. The line says «митр. Загребского» and «исп», and the name page «митрополит Загребский, исповедник», which agree, so `metropolitan`, `hierarch` and `confessor` are the source’s own words; THE OFFICE IS STORED AS THE BARE «Metropolitan», because the locale packs carry no «Metropolitan of Zagreb» and BRIEF-ADDENDUM §4 forbids minting one — the see is in the life instead. HE IS A SERBIAN HIERARCH ON A RUSSIAN DAY and the corpus’s Serbian wave has not reached him: a Cyrillic grep for «Васич» over every `saint.json` returns nothing, `ls -d saints/dositheus*` returns `dositheus-kolchenkov`, `dositheus-of-verkhny-ostrov` and `dositheus-the-obedient`, none of them this man, and `fk.mjs` on the stored form returns NONE. The russian row is therefore the only venerated row this folder gets, and the serbian row is left `undocumented` with its note saying the Prologue was not checked. The day page prints one hymn only, a kontakion of the venerable Melania, and nothing under this name.
